case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh and Others v Ramesh Chandra Bajpai
petitioner: State of Madhya Pradesh and Others
respondent:
Ramesh Chandra Bajpai
Supreme Court of India

28 July 2009
Civil Appeal No. of 2009(Arising out of S.L.P.(C) No. 25682 of 2008)
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
1.   The State of Madhya Pradesh is before us aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 4.1.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Indore Bench at Indore in Writ Appeal No.201 of 2006 whereby and where under the appeal preferred by the appellant herein from a judgment and order dated 3.11.2004 passed by a learned Single Judge of the said High Court in Writ Petition No.4005/2003, was dismissed.
2.   The core question which arises for consideration before us is as to whether the respondent herein who is working as Physical Training Instructor in Government Ayurvedic College is entitled to claim parity of pay with the teachers who have been granted UGC scale of pay.
3.   The respondent was appointed as Physical Training Instruct
facts: The State of Madhya Pradesh is before us aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 4.1.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Indore Bench at Indore in Writ Appeal No.201 of 2006 whereby and where under the appeal preferred by the appellant herein from a judgment and order dated 3.11.2004 passed by a learned Single Judge of the said High Court in Writ Petition No.4005/2003, was dismissed.
The respondent was appointed as Physical Training Instructor in Government Ayurvedic College, Ujjain by an offer of appointment dated 18.1.1973.

He filed O.A. No.907 of 1998 before the Madhya Pradesh Administrative Tribunal, Indore Bench (for short, 'the Tribunal') with the prayer that the non-applicants in the O.A. (the petitioners herein) be directed to treat him as teacher and fix his pay in the pay scale prescribed for that post along with the benefit of senior scale and also give him the UGC pay scale (Rs.3,700-5,700) w.e.f.1.1.1986.

The Tribunal dismissed the application of the respondent observing that the applicant having not been holding the post of Sports Officer and having not been working in the Government College administered by the Department of Higher Education, he was not entitled to any relief.
issues: Whether the respondent is entitled to claim parity of pay with the teachers who have been granted UGC scale of pay.

Whether the High Court committed serious error by relying upon the ratio of the judgment in P.S. Ramamohana Rao v. A.P. Agricultural University and another [1997 (8) SCC 350] 1997 Indlaw SC 2029 for the purpose of granting relief to the respondent.
petitioner_arguments: The State Government has not issued any order equating the post of Physical Training Instructor with that of teacher.
Recruitment to the posts of Physical Training Instructors and Sports Officers are regulated by different sets of rules.
Holders of the two posts cannot be treated at par for the purpose of fixation of pay in the UGC scale.
respondent_arguments: After having accepted and implemented the orders passed by the Tribunal and the High Court in the cases of other Physical Training Instructors for grant of UGC scale of pay, it is not open to the appellants to discriminate the respondent by relying upon the provisions of the 1987 Rules.

The Physical Training Instructors appointed in Medical Colleges of the State have been granted the benefit of UGC scale of pay and submitted that the High Court did not commit any error by directing the petitioners to fix the respondent's pay in the UGC scale.
court_reasoning: It is well settled that the doctrine of equal pay for equal work can be invoked only when the employees are similarly situated.
Similarity in the designation or nature or quantum of work is not determinative of equality in the matter of pay scales.

The Court has to consider the factors like the source and mode of recruitment/appointment, qualifications, the nature of work, the value thereof, responsibilities, reliability, experience, confidentiality, functional need, etc.
holding: We hold that the approach adopted by the learned Single Judge and Division Bench is clearly erroneous.
The doctrine of equal pay for equal work can be invoked only when the employees are similarly situated.

The Court has to consider the factors like the source and mode of recruitment/appointment, qualifications, the nature of work, the value thereof, responsibilities, reliability, experience, confidentiality, functional need, etc.
